A search engine for 15 years of greentext.

Greptext is a multimodal search engine over 123,183 screenshots from r/greentext (2011–2026): OCR reads the stories, a vision-language model reads the memes, and multimodal search with grounded answering sits on top of the result.

SEARCH ROUTES · STORY / MEME / VISUAL
>01 · THE PROBLEM

Why greentexts are hard for machines

A greentext post is a single screenshot with two different things inside it: a story (rendered green text, dense, sometimes hundreds of lines) and a reaction meme (an image whose meaning is cultural, not textual). Nothing separates them, no metadata, no layout guarantees, no separate files. Any search over this corpus has to read the story and recognize the meme out of the same pixels.

Three properties make this genuinely awkward, and the whole architecture follows from taking them seriously:

>01
The text fights OCR.

Low-contrast green-on-dark rendering, screenshot compression artifacts, and stylized fonts.

>02
The images fight resizing.

Some posts are multi-panel conversation sequences thousands of pixels tall. Height-capping destroys them; only width may ever be capped.

>03
The meme fights embeddings.

A whole-image embedding of any greentext is dominated by “green text on dark background.” Every post looks like every other post; the meme barely moves the vector. Naive CLIP-style search collapses.

>02 · DATA FORENSICS

The corpus, and what auditing it revealed

The raw material is a Pushshift-derived dump of 224,559 r/greentext posts spanning August 2011 to March 2026, joined to 123,183 surviving image files (127,009 posts still had images; the ~3,826 gap is exact-URL reposts sharing one file on disk, a detail that later mattered for pipeline correctness). Auditing before processing paid off twice.

upvote_ratio carries no signal. It is 1.0 across every record: that is simply the default a post carries the moment it is uploaded, and these snapshots were never updated afterwards. As a reception measure it is unusable; only score and num_comments are usable.

>03 · SYSTEM

Architecture at a glance

Two extraction pipelines run over every image and never talk to each other until the end. Piece 1 reads the story, OCR plus cleanup, producing one clean transcript per post. Piece 2 sees the meme, a vision-language model producing structured JSON: what meme it is, where it sits, and how it relates to the story.

Their outputs feed three search indices behind one retrieval interface. Images themselves are served from object storage, so the interface stays lightweight enough to run anywhere.

                123,183 screenshots
                 /              \
    PIECE 1: READ            PIECE 2: SEE
PaddleOCR (band tiling)    Qwen3-VL-32B (vLLM)
→ rules cleanup            → template name (controlled vocab)
→ LLM cleanup (~10%)       → bounding box, relationship, fit
→ transcript per post      → meme crop → DINOv2 embedding
                 \              /
              THREE SEARCH ROUTES
    story text · meme identity · visual similarity
                      |
          retrieval interface (Gradio)
          images served from Cloudflare R2
>04 · PIECE 1

Reading the story

OCR is PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv6), with band tiling for tall images: very long screenshots are sliced into overlapping horizontal bands so the recognizer never sees more than it can handle, then line results are merged geometrically. Cleanup is split deliberately in two:

1, A deterministic rules stage (regex + geometric line merging) handles the bulk: reply-link stripping, line reassembly, artifact removal. It re-runs over the whole corpus in seconds, which means any fix discovered later is retroactively free.

2, An LLM stage only for flagged residue (12,480 items, 10.1% of the corpus): items the rules stage marks as suspicious go to a small VLM (Qwen3-VL-4B via vLLM) for repair. Continuous batching turned a projected overnight HF-transformers run into under an hour.

Only what can’t be done deterministically gets a model. Everything a model touches is flagged, resumable, and auditable.

>05 · PIECE 2

Seeing the meme

A 32-billion-parameter vision-language model (Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, FP8, served via vLLM) looks at every post and returns structured JSON: the meme’s template name, its bounding box (normalized 0–1000), its denotation (what is literally shown), its connotation (what it means culturally), a relationship type, reaction, topical, format, irrelevant, or none, and a fit rating with rationale. Two decisions carry this stage:

Controlled vocabulary. Free-text meme labels don’t retrieve, “Chad”, “Gigachad”, and “the Chad face” are three different strings to a text embedder. The VLM picks from a fixed template list or returns other plus a free-form description. Misnamed templates still happen; they’re logged as failure material, not hidden.

Bounding boxes make visual search possible. The box crops the meme out of the composite, and the crop, not the whole screenshot, is embedded with DINOv2. That sidesteps the “everything looks like green text on black” collapse. The same boxes also retroactively clean OCR output: text inside a meme region can be masked out of transcripts after the fact, because cleanup is deterministic and re-runs are free.

>06 · RETRIEVAL

Search: three routes into the corpus

Greptext answers three different questions, and a fourth route makes the case for the other three: plain whole-image SigLIP search, on its own, retrieves “greentext-ness”, not stories or memes. Routes are combined with a tunable α-fusion; retrieval is cosine similarity; results render in a Gradio interface with thumbnails from object storage and full resolution on click.

>07 · ENGINEERING

Serving & engineering constraints

STORAGE

Images live on Cloudflare R2, public bucket, zero egress fees, ~$0.22/month for 24.6 GB. GitHub rejected (LFS quotas; a repo is not a blob store). Google Drive rejected (per-file latency, public-link quota bans). A resumable 32-worker uploader treats the bucket itself as the source of truth.

BUILD VS BUY

Building locally was the far cheaper option: a frontier-API captioning pass over 123k images would have cost hundreds of dollars and still couldn’t return croppable meme regions. Local models do both halves, OCR the easy part and the VLM the hard part, for electricity. Total cloud spend to date: $0.14 of Cloudflare R2 storage.

HARDWARE
RTX 5070 Ti · 16 GB, light inference
RTX 5090 · 32 GB, shared workstation
RTX 6000 BLACKWELL · 96 GB, heavy passes

All under WSL2, which cost real debugging time: sm_120 needs cu128 wheels (torch ≥ 2.7), vLLM needs VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0, and missing UVA support silently changes which model/engine combos even start.

>08 · FAILURES, KEPT ON PURPOSE

When the machine mis-sees

Systems that look at things get things wrong. The interesting part is how.

Silent truncation beats no one.
SYMPTOMHF path quietly cut OCR inputs at 8,192 tokens, shortened transcripts, no error
CAUSEunbounded input; the vLLM port crashed on the same items, the crash was the gift
FIXhard cap on the pipeline’s one unbounded input, applied loudly
Whole-image embeddings see the genre, not the content.
SYMPTOMevery greentext embeds as “green text on dark background”
CAUSEthe meme occupies a corner; the genre dominates the vector
FIXcrop memes via VLM bboxes; embed the crop (DINOv2)
Duplicate filenames, colliding IDs.
SYMPTOMcolliding crop IDs in the verification run
CAUSE3,826 exact-URL reposts share files; iteration ran over manifest rows, not unique files
FIXunique-file iteration everywhere
The validator lied first.
SYMPTOMmisleadingly low similarity minima in validation
CAUSEdifflib’s autojunk heuristic, the measurement was buggy before the pipeline was
FIXautojunk disabled; validator validated
The VLM invents memes.
SYMPTOMniche, regional, or post-cutoff templates get misnamed
CAUSEcultural knowledge has a training cutoff too
FIXcontrolled vocabulary contains the damage; misnames are logged, not laundered
One image was a bomb.
SYMPTOMa ~100-megapixel decompression bomb sat waiting for a naive Image.open()
CAUSE15 years of the internet contains everything
FIXpixel-count guard before decode; the pipeline survives
Version pins are essential.
SYMPTOMa multi-GPU NCCL failure that turned out to be irrelevant noise for single-device inference, the red herring cost more time than the real bugs
FIXPaddlePaddle pinned to 3.2.2 (3.3.x ships a CPU-inference regression); transformers pinned per stack
>09 · BEYOND THE BRIEF

The research question

Piece 2 doesn’t just label memes, it rates how well each meme fits its story. That turns the corpus into a dataset for a question the assignment never asked: do posters who match memes to stories better get rewarded with higher scores?

The ingredients exist: fit ratings and relationship types per post, a score trust map from the corpus audit, and a rescraper that adds removed_by_category (to exclude moderation-killed posts) plus a uniform measurement timestamp across all crawl vintages. The regression itself is future work, the pipeline was built so it wouldn’t have to be rebuilt when the question gets asked.

      |         + removed_by_category

>10 · WORKFLOW

The complete pipeline, end to end

One convention holds everything together: every stage reads and writes JSONL keyed on imgname, and every output file doubles as its own progress record, restart any stage after a crash and it resumes where it stopped. Stages 00–03 are piece 1 (Windows, "Wednesday"); 04–06 are piece 2 (WSL2 on the workstation); 07–08 assemble and serve.

00 MANIFEST One clean table from the raw dump: 224,559 posts, 127,009 with an image URL, 123,183 unique files on disk (24.6 GB). The i.redd.it filename becomes the join key for every later stage.
01 OCR PaddleOCR over band-tiled screenshots (1,600 px bands, 200 px overlap, midline-ownership dedup); every detected line keeps its x/y coordinates. ~1.5 s/image on CPU, sharded across two machines.
02 RULES Deterministic cleanup: regex removes machine-generated 4chan chrome; geometry (median line gap, 1.6× threshold) reassembles wrapped lines and paragraph breaks. Whole corpus in under a minute; 12,480 items (10.1%) flagged as residue.
02b LLM Qwen3-VL-4B repairs only the flagged residue: 11,803 repairs accepted, 97 rejected as degenerate (repetition × inflation), 580 near-empty items skipped by the anti-hallucination guard.
03 MERGE Rules stay authoritative; trusted LLM output overrides flagged rows → greentext_final.jsonl, 123,181 transcripts, each row carrying its source and flags.
, GATE Word-level similarity against a 7,925-image Qwen3-VL gold set: mean 0.945, median 1.000, 7.2% below 0.80, and the worst diffs were read by hand before the full run was trusted.
04 VLM PASS Qwen3-VL-32B-FP8 (vLLM, 96 GB card) sees each image plus its transcript and returns structured JSON: up to four meme bounding boxes (normalized 0–1000), template name, denotation/connotation, relationship type, fit rating. Memes found in 106,456 images (86.4%).
05 CROP+EMBED Normalized boxes re-projected onto the full-resolution originals; area/aspect sanity gates reject grounding failures; 105,656 accepted crops (85.8%) get pHash + DINOv2-large embeddings.
06 MASK OCR lines inside accepted meme boxes are dropped (format posts exempt; a ≤50% proportionality guard protects stories from oversized boxes), then the deterministic rules re-run the whole corpus in seconds, retroactive fixes are free.
07 INDEX SigLIP whole-image embeddings (123,181 · 100%) and MiniLM story-text embeddings; everything validated into one bundle and uploaded to Cloudflare R2.
08 SERVE A Gradio notebook on a free Colab T4 runs three routes, story text, meme identity, visual similarity, fused with a tunable α; thumbnails stream from R2.
>11 · NOTEBOOK

The serving layer: one Colab notebook

Everything heavy happened offline (section 10). What ships to the course is a single notebook on a free Colab runtime: it downloads a ~730 MB verified index bundle once into Drive, and from then on a query is encode → one matrix–vector product over 123k rows → render. The corpus is never re-embedded; no model ever touches it again. Retrieval is pure numpy and runs on CPU, only the answering stage wants the GPU.

0 SETUP Installs, Drive mount (the bundle’s persistent cache, one download survives every runtime reset), the R2 manifest URL, and the answering config: Gemma 3 4B in nf4 4-bit, fusion default α = 0.60, top-k 4, one grounding image per answer.
1 LOADER The manifest is two things at once: a table of contents (which file, which role, which model produced it) and an integrity contract (sha256 + size per file). Per artifact: download → hash-verify → load → row-order check against the canonical id list → widen fp16 to fp32. Masks mark rows with no valid vector; they score −∞ and can never rank.
2 BUNDLE The only cell that touches the network for corpus data. First run ~730 MB, every later run hash checks only; prints shapes, per-space valid counts, pinned model strings and one spot-check row.
3 ENCODERS The query-side models are pinned by the manifest: encoder ids are read from the bundle, so a query vector can never come from a different checkpoint than the corpus vectors it is compared against. MiniLM + SigLIP load eagerly; DINOv2 and Gemma prefetch to disk but stay out of memory until first use.
4 RETRIEVAL Five routes · STORY TEXT, MEME IDENTITY, SIGLIP, HYBRID, VISUAL SIM, one mechanism: encode the query, score all 123k rows in a single BLAS call (single-digit milliseconds), mask, min-max normalize, and for HYBRID fuse α·siglip + (1−α)·story.
5 ANSWERING Grounded generation: the top retrieved image is fetched from R2 and placed into Gemma’s context next to its caption line, the model answers from what it can see, not from OCR alone. On a CPU runtime, or on any failure, the pipeline degrades to retrieval-only: answering can never take search down.
7 UI SHARED Every panel is built as HTML strings: result cards, the debug console (each pipeline stage logs what it did and how long it took), corpus statistics computed live from the masks, and the shared pipeline generator that streams stages into the interface as they finish.
8 ATLAS The workstation-precomputed UMAP of each embedding space, drawn on a raw canvas: 123k points cross the Python→JS bridge once as typed arrays; masked rows are filtered server-side; clicking a point resolves the nearest neighbor client-side and opens the inspector through Gradio’s server-function bridge.
9 INTERFACE Gradio Blocks, two views behind a brand top bar: the dashboard (mode rail on the left, results in the center under a live fusion bar, search panel with example queries on the right) and the full-bleed atlas. Moving α or TOP_K re-runs the last query and re-ranks the results in place; uploading an image auto-selects VISUAL SIM.
10 LAUNCH Queue + share link, fullscreen in its own tab; the public URL is kept private (4chan-derived corpus, anything published is hand-curated).
>12 · DISCLOSURE

AI assistance & content note

AI use in this project is disclosed on two separate levels: models running inside the system, and models used to build it.

IN THE SYSTEM

PaddleOCR (text detection), Qwen3-VL-4B (repair of 12,480 flagged transcripts), Qwen3-VL-32B (meme analysis), DINOv2 / SigLIP / MiniLM (embeddings). Their outputs are treated as measurements, not truths: flagged, gated against a 7,925-image gold set, and audited, see 08 · MIS-SEEING.

IN THE BUILDING

Pipeline code, architecture decisions and this documentation were developed in iterative dialogue with LLM assistants (Anthropic Claude). Problem framing, design decisions, data auditing and all final judgments are the author's; assistant-drafted code and text were reviewed, tested and corrected before use. Every quantitative claim on this page traces to pipeline output files, not to model prose.

CONTENT

The corpus is public r/greentext posts (a Pushshift-derived dump plus a live-API rescrape), used here for coursework and research. Authorship of the underlying posts remains with their original posters; the corpus itself is not redistributed. Documentation shows hand-picked SFW examples only.
